subject: URGENT: Cascade Payments — Hosted API p95/p99 regression impacting transactions

From: Rachael Park <rachael.park@cascadepay.com>

Cc: Michael Donovan <michael.donovan@cascadepay.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — Cascade Payments noticed p95/p99 regressions

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a major degradation in checkout latency around 08:40 PDT this morning. p95 across our integration jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s and p99 is spiking above 3s. We are also seeing an uptick in 502/503 errors and dropped payment requests (~2% of requests in last 20m). This is directly impacting volume — merchants are retrying and some transactions fail.

We are on your hosted API (region: us-west-2) using model-id: redwood-llama-v1-16k-q4. No recent config changes on our end. Can you confirm whether you are seeing any platform-wide regressions or if this is isolated to our tenant? We need an ETA on mitigation and whether there's anything we should change client-side.

Please escalate — our CRO has asked for an executive summary in 30 minutes.

— Rachael

Joining now. Early noise from metrics: host-level GPU mem fragmentation (slab churn) in the us-west-2 hosted pool correlates with time of regression. Seeing increased KV cache eviction and repeated GC-style allocations. No full node restart yet.

I will pull diagnostics: per-request KV cache hits, per-stream kernel wait times, and recent allocation traces. If we confirm fragmentation-driven OOMs, mitigation options: burst routing away from affected pools; fall back to quantized 8-bit runtime/build; or route to a warmed cold-variant with smaller KV working set.

— Marcus (runtime)

Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 09:33:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — Cascade Payments noticed p95/p99 regressions

On bridge. Observed: repeated per-GPU allocation failures followed by successful restarts of the runtime service on several hosts in the shared hosted pool. Logs show OOM kills of inference workers and subsequent scheduling churn. There are transient 503s while requests drain.

Immediate mitigation applied: we enabled a model-variant fallback policy for Cascade Payments (redirected to redwood-llama-v1-16k-q4-lite) — should reduce per-request memory usage ~30%. Also raised routing weight to dedicated healthy hosts in us-west-2 to reduce probability of hitting fragmented hosts.

Requesting the following from the customer: recent request IDs for failed transactions (we logged 6 sample request-ids in the bridge notes) and permission to enable short-term rate limiting if errors continue.

— Connor (SRE)

Subject: Exec summary (for Cascade Payments board/CRO) — immediate actions and ETA

Short exec summary for your CRO/board:
- Impact: Hosted API region us-west-2 experienced GPU memory fragmentation leading to worker OOMs. Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency and a small increase in 502/503 errors affecting a subset of tenants, including Cascade Payments.
- Mitigation applied: temporary model-variant fallback deployed for Cascade Payments (redwood-llama-v1-16k-q4 -> redwood-llama-v1-16k-q4-lite), routing to healthier hosts in the pool, and enabling conservative client-side retry guidance. Immediate effect: p95 reduced from ~1.6s to ~600ms; p99 reduced from ~3s to ~1.4s for sampled traffic.
- Next actions: engineering to collect KV cache dumps + kernel allocation traces (ETA 6 hours), SRE to mark affected hosts cordoned for maintenance and live-defrag procedures (ETA 4 hours), and product to prepare permanent model-variant recommendation if workload needs sustained capacity.
- Business ask: we recommend a 24-hour credit for affected volume; our CS rep (Evelyn) will coordinate.

I'll follow up with a technical RCA within 48 hours and a remediation timeline. Please let me know if you need a one-page note formatted for external merchant comms.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_bridge_notes.pdf (internal bridge notes, mitigation commands run), captures_kv_dumps.tar.gz (KV cache snapshots), dcos_stacktrace.txt (collected stack traces)

Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 13:05:09 -07:00
Subject: Post-mortem snapshot — evidence of slab fragmentation and remediation plan

Team — quick snapshot while we prepare the full RCA. Findings so far:
- Root cause signal: increased slab fragmentation on a subset of GPU hosts in the shared hosted pool. Frequent kernel path swaps and KV cache churn mean working sets exceeded compacting thresholds, triggering allocation failures and per-worker OOMs.
- Why Cascade was impacted: their traffic pattern (many mid-length sequences with repeated prompt prefixes) raised KV working set pressure. The particular hosts serving their tenant had degraded allocator fragmentation metrics from a prior noisy workload.
- Temporary measures that helped:
  * Model-variant fallback (q4 -> q4-lite) reduced per-request memory and lowered p95/p99 as observed.
  * Routing away from fragmented hosts reduced error rate.
  * Short-term client-side retry guidance reduced compounding retries.
- Longer-term remediation: targeted live-defrag tooling in runtime (scheduled), host-level allocator improvements (Q3 release), and adding per-tenant memory isolation heuristics to reduce noisy neighbor impact.

I'll attach the collection pointers and a timeline for the remediation. Full RCA with traces + timeline targeted EOD Monday.

— Marcus Lin
Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
